title: racoonctl status JSON output
description: Wire format produced by `racoonctl status -f json` (see racoonctl(1) and doc/dev/racoonctl-status-analysis.md, issues #139/#140). Describes the current schema_version 1.1 only -- per the project's own additive-minor/breaking-major policy (D4), this file is updated in place on future minor bumps rather than kept per-version; a breaking (major) change gets a new file instead. Field inventory and types verified directly against src/racoon/status.c's json_render_ph1()/json_render_ph2(), not against the analysis doc, to catch any drift between what was decided and what actually ships.

schema_version.description: "major.minor" (D4). Additive changes bump minor only; this file is scoped to exactly 1.1's field set.

phase2.description: Present only when the request used -v/--verbose (status.c render_json()); absent entirely, not an empty array, on a non-verbose request.

state.description: status.c ph1_state_name() -- closed set, every case (including the default) returns a fixed literal, verified directly from the switch statement.

version.description: ISAKMP major.minor decoded from the wire version byte's two nibbles (status.c collect_ph1()).

exchange_mode.description: "MAIN"/"AGGRESSIVE"/"BASE" for the three known exchange types (status.c exchange_mode_name()); any other exchange type falls back to strnames.c's s_isakmp_etype(), an open name-table lookup -- not a closed enum, deliberately not hardcoded here (see the schema's top-level description on x-source annotations vs. guessed enums).

dh_group.description: Deliberately a JSON string, not integer, matching the actual wire render -- see the top-level description's note on not 'fixing' this to look more consistent than the wire format actually is. Compare phase2[].proposal.pfs_group/effective_group, which are genuinely integers.

username.description: null if XAuth is in progress but no username has been received yet (status.c collect_xauth(): dupstr() of a possibly-NULL source pointer). Deliberately never the password (H-3, issue #139).

generate_policy.description: status.c generate_policy_name() -- closed set, default case also returns a fixed literal ("none").

index.description: "0x" + 8 hex digits (the phase2 msgid), status.c collect_ph2().

phase1_index.description: D6, issue #140: the parent phase1[].index, same cookie_pair_hex() format, letting a consumer join the two arrays. null only in the brief window where iph2->ph1 is unbound (unbindph12(), called from initph2() and during phase2 teardown) while the handle is still enumerable -- verified reachable, not hypothetical.

state.description: status.c ph2_state_name() -- closed set, same verification basis as phase1[].state.

spi_in.description: Top 16 bits of the real SPI, rest masked (status.c mask_spi()) -- never the full SPI, by design. The \? alternative is asprintf()'s own OOM fallback (status.c), included for honesty about the actual wire contract rather than only describing the common case.

protocol.description: status.c ph2_protocol_name() -- closed set, default case returns a fixed literal.

encmode.description: strnames.c s_ipsecdoi_encmode() -- an open name-table lookup with a numeric-string fallback (num2str()) for any value not in its table, so deliberately not enumerated as a closed set here even though every value seen in practice is one of Any/Tunnel/Transport/UDP-Tunnel/UDP-Transport.

src.description: CIDR, e.g. "203.0.113.1/32" (status.c sockaddr_to_cidr()); real negotiated prefix length from getspbyspid() when available, else host-width default.

protocol.description: The wire selector's proto_id (struct ipsecdoi_id_b), or the literal "any" when unset.

compression_algorithm.description: Present only when negotiated (status.c: proto->proto_id == IPSECDOI_PROTO_IPCOMP), confirmed live and reachable, not a documented future gap.

pfs_group.description: null when PFS was not negotiated at the phase2 level. A null here does not mean no DH group protects the tunnel -- see effective_group.

effective_group.description: D6, issue #140: equals pfs_group when PFS was negotiated; otherwise the parent phase1's dh_group, per RFC 2409 SS5.5 (Phase 2 KEYMAT without a PFS exchange of its own is derived entirely from SKEYID_d, which comes from the parent Phase 1's DH exchange). Deliberately always a JSON number, never null or a string, in both branches -- see the type-consistency rule in doc/dev/racoonctl-status-analysis.md's D6 entry. 0 marks the rare case where the parent phase1 handle was unbound (see phase1_index) and no PFS was negotiated either, making the value genuinely indeterminate; 0 is not a valid real DH group id.
